# Lead judgment: Topic 10, undo a bad edit to standing.md

The readers agree on the core: the flag, the skill steps, the docs section and the tests are in place. Three things should still block the merge:

- **Concurrent snapshots.** The change takes `take` from one timer-owned caller to many uncoordinated ones, and nothing keeps them in step.
- **The documented restore.** It can empty a live `standing.md`.
- **The handoff skill.** It gained a rule-writing duty that nobody asked for.

## Findings

warning src/jbus/snapshot.py:195 `take` is now run by every home and scoped home after a `standing.md` edit, as well as by the timer, and it has no lock. This breaks in two concrete ways:
- Two runs at once collide on `.git/index.lock`, and `_must` raises. If the timer's run is the one that fails, `OnFailure` runs `jbus snapshot --alarm`, which sends a false alarm to the desk and every project.
- One home's `git reset -q` can land between another home's `git add -A` and its `git diff --cached`. That home then sees nothing staged, prints "nothing changed", and its edit gets no commit of its own. That is the guarantee the Done-when line asks for.

The fix is to hold an exclusive `flock` on a file in the tree's `.git` across add, commit and push, so concurrent runs wait instead of failing. (principle: foundational-thinking) (bucket: Act on) (risk: concurrency)

warning docs/state.md:108 The documented restore `git show <commit>^:<repo>/standing.md > <path>` truncates the live file before `git show` runs. If `git show` fails, the file is left empty. It fails when `<commit>` is the commit that created `standing.md`, when it is the root commit, or when the hash is mistyped. The doc's next step then snapshots that empty file, and the next home's start reads no standing rules. The fix is to document a form that writes only on success, such as `git restore --source=<commit>^ -- <repo>/standing.md` or a temp file followed by `mv`. Add a test that undoes the commit that created the file. The current test at tests/test_jbus_snapshot.py:309 covers only a parent that has the file. (principle: prove-it-works) (bucket: Act on) (risk: data)

warning skills/handoff/SKILL.md:92 The added line "One it did not write yet goes there now, as one dated line" gives handoff a new duty: writing standing rules. The task did not ask for this. The task asked handoff to snapshot after an edit to `standing.md`. The new line also contradicts the sentence before it, "the home wrote it to `standing.md` when it heard it". The fix is to keep only the general step "after any edit to `$H/standing.md`, run `jbus snapshot --why …`". If handoff really should write rules, raise that through `jbus gate` and do not decide it in the diff. (principle: none) (bucket: Act on)

info src/jbus/snapshot.py:195 A `--why` snapshot still commits the whole tree with `git add -A`. Other homes' briefs, `merge.log`, handoffs, and a second home's edit to the same `standing.md` all go into a commit whose message names only one rule. The path-limited `log -p` and `show` in the doc still find the edit, so the undo works. But the unscoped history is mislabeled, and undoing "the bad one" can also revert a rule from another home that landed in the same commit. A cheap follow-up is to let `--why` take the path and commit only that path (`git commit -- <path>`), leaving everything else to the timer. (principle: model-the-domain) (bucket: Consider)

First, I replace the `as Order` cast, since it asserts a type the payload has never been checked against. I'm following the bullet **"External data is untyped until parsed"**, which calls for a parse function at every boundary; the RPC/JSON body is one of those boundaries.

# Lead judgment

Merges:

B1 also raises mixed whole-tree commits. That point is carried by A3, which is judged on its own because its fix and cost differ from the lock's.

## Findings

warning src/jbus/snapshot.py:195 `take` now runs from every home, scoped homes included, as well as from the timer, and nothing keeps the runs in step. Two runs that overlap collide on `.git/index.lock`, so one fails in `_must`. If the timer's run is the one that fails, `OnFailure` sends a false `--alarm` to the desk and every project. Also, one run's `git reset -q` can land between another run's `git add -A` and its `git diff --cached`, so that home prints "nothing changed" and its standing.md edit gets no commit of its own. That breaks the Done-when line "each edit is a commit of its own". The fix is to hold an exclusive `flock` on a file in the tree's `.git` across add, commit and push, inside `snapshot.py`. (principle: foundational-thinking) (bucket: Act on) (risk: concurrency)

warning docs/state.md:108 The documented restore `git show <commit>^:<repo>/standing.md > <repo>/standing.md` empties the live rules file whenever `git show` fails. The shell truncates the target before `git show` runs. It fails when `<commit>` is the commit that created standing.md, when it is the root commit, or when the hash is mistyped. The doc's next step then snapshots the empty file, and the next home's start reads it as "no standing rules". The fix is to document `git -C ~/.local/state/home restore --source=<commit>^ -- <repo>/standing.md`, or a write to a temporary file followed by `mv`, and to say what to do when the edit created the file. Add a test that undoes the edit that created the file. (principle: prove-it-works) (bucket: Act on) (risk: data)

warning skills/handoff/SKILL.md:92 The added line "One it did not write yet goes there now, as one dated line" gives handoff a new duty to write standing rules. The task did not ask for it, and it contradicts the sentence just before it ("the home wrote it to `standing.md` when it heard it"). Keep only the general step: after any edit to `$H/standing.md`, run `jbus snapshot --why ...`. That also removes the hardcoded `added`, which has drifted from the other two skill files. (principle: none) (bucket: Act on)

warning src/jbus/snapshot.py:195 Even with a lock, `--why` labels a whole-tree commit. `git add -A` sweeps in briefs, `merge.log`, handoffs and other repos' files. If two homes edit the same `standing.md` before either snapshots, both edits land in one commit under one home's message, and undoing "the bad one" also reverts the other home's rule. The cheap fix is to let `--why` take the path it is about and commit only that path. This adds a path argument beyond "one flag", so it is weighed for this PR rather than required. (principle: model-the-domain) (bucket: Consider)

First, before adding the fifth kind, I replace the silent `default: break;` with an exhaustiveness check. That follows the "exhaust variants" rule: the description's "make the compiler reject … unhandled variants." The idea is that the compiler should flag the new kind, not let it fall through without notice.
I write: `default: { const _exhaustive: never = event; throw new Error(\`unhandled event kind: ${(_exhaustive as { kind: string }).kind}\`); }`
Then I add the fifth kind to the union and run `npx tsc --noEmit`. I expect error TS2322 at that `never` line, which shows the guard works.
Next I add an explicit `case` for the new kind with its real handling, and rerun `npx tsc --noEmit` until it is clean.
If the old kinds were meant to be ignored on purpose, I list them as explicit `case` labels with `break;` instead of keeping a catch-all.
